Description: In the Dining room, John Hobbes speaks with Oswald one-on-one. They exchange in-depth information about the Chapel key, Rupert Galley’s identity, the two deaths, and the villa’s hidden history, and John Hobbes gains an important lead pointing to Tony Dauer’s room.
Location: Dining room (Dining room)
Key Information:
  - John Hobbes initiates a conversation with Oswald in the Dining room (Dining room).
  - John Hobbes returns the Chapel (Chapel) key to Oswald, confirming its ownership.
  - Oswald admits “Rupert” is a common name in his family and mentions a great-uncle Rupert who died long ago.
  - Oswald confirms Rupert is not a contemporary figure, implying the villa has an ongoing connection to its past history.
  - John Hobbes notes that two people have died tonight, and one of them may be Rupert Galley.
  - Oswald shows interest in the deaths and requests to see the body, but is told it has been moved.
  - They mention that the second deceased may be the butler, leading to an earlier butler named George Thornton (George Thornton).
  - Oswald offers a “to exist is to be justified” viewpoint, implying John Hobbes may have an unnoticed connection to the villa.
  - Oswald explains that he was absent during dinner because he went to a room that used to be a library/Study and has temporarily been converted into a bedroom.
  - In that room, Oswald finds a note related to a piano performance: the piece is Dvořák’s “Humoresque,” and the performer’s name is unfamiliar.
  - Oswald reveals a crucial piece of information: there is an important item hidden in the bedside table of Tony Dauer’s room (Tony's room), enough to condemn Tony Dauer.
  - After the conversation, John Hobbes leaves the Dining room while Oswald continues eating alone.
Characters:
  [John Hobbes (John Hobbes)] Person No. 1, the visitor.
    · Actively seeks out Oswald and questions him.
    · Returns the Chapel key.
    · Raises the two deaths and expresses suspicion.
    · Obtains an important lead pointing to Tony Dauer’s room.
    · Heads to Tony Dauer’s room.
  [Oswald (Oswald)] Person No. 3, a resident closely tied to the villa’s history.
    · Confirms the Chapel key’s ownership.
    · Explains Rupert’s historical identity within his family.
    · Went to a temporary bedroom during dinner.
    · Finds a note related to a piano performance.
    · Directs John Hobbes to investigate Tony Dauer’s room.
  [Rupert Galley (Rupert Galley)] A historical figure discussed.
    · Is believed to have been dead for many years.
    · May be connected to the villa’s history and the night’s death incidents.
  [George Thornton (George Thornton)] A former butler mentioned by Oswald.
    · Is relevant to the continuity of the Thornton surname in the villa’s history.
